title: Mission 19: before/after hardening checklist
rows: Incoming firewall
Inactive in the initial Mission 19 baseline (attempt 1).
Active; default deny incoming; allow outgoing; management SSH allowed.
Reduce unsolicited reachability. Initial log, latest firewall status and successful local SSH provide evidence.
Worker identity
The controlled teaching service runs as root (UID 0).
The same worker runs as nobody (UID 65534).
Remove unneeded root authority. Runtime credentials are captured before and after.
Worker confinement
NoNewPrivileges=no; ProtectSystem=no.
NoNewPrivileges=yes; ProtectSystem=strict; runtime NoNewPrivs=1.
Prevent new privilege and broad filesystem writes. Configuration and live process fields agree.
Worker resources
MemoryMax=infinity.
MemoryMax=67108864 bytes (64 MiB); TasksMax=16.
Limit availability impact. The final systemd properties record the configured bounds.
Ordinary new-file access
Controlled child-shell umask 0022 produces an ordinary file at mode 0644.
Loading the project umask 0077 produces an ordinary file at mode 0600.
Reduce unintended sharing. Both files are created with touch, not mktemp, inside a private test directory.
Package state
The earlier audit recorded four deferred utility updates.
0 pending packages listed in the final captured inventory.
Install available updates and record the real package state; never infer patching from apt update alone.
baseline_note: The initial firewall baseline is preserved in mission-19/attempt-1.log. Service-before and verified-after observations come from the latest Mission 19 attempt. The umask comparison is a deliberately controlled fixture, not a claim that the original login shell used 0022. Repeated runs can begin with UFW already active.
rollback: Restore the SECURELAB-CLEAN stopped-disk recovery copy for a full reversal. scripts/rollback_hardening.sh restores the recorded UFW files/state and removes the lab worker and umask policy; it does not undo package upgrades.
